thread:
customer-rep: Hey team — Acme (enterprise) reports their onboarding JSON parser started failing right after the canary swap to r-inf-v3p4-canary at ~2026-03-10T12:07Z. Error from their service: "Unexpected token , in JSON at position 123". They included the raw response they received:

customer-rep: ```json
{"id": "resp_01", "items": [{"name": "widget", "qty": 3}],}
```

customer-rep: It looks like there is a trailing comma and an extra top-level wrapper sometimes. This is blocking onboarding flow. Can support/eng triage? cc @eva

eva: Thanks — investigating. Can you paste the trace_id and exact model alias they hit? Also want the timestamped request log if available.

customer-rep: Trace: tr-8a9f2c4b. Model: r-inf-v3p4-canary. Will DM logs but here's the API request they used (sanitized):

customer-rep: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"r-inf-v3p4-canary","input":"generate structured order","json_mode":"strict"}'
```

matt: Looking at the trace — the runtime emitted two patterns: sometimes it wraps payload in a top-level "response" key, other times it streams array chunks and reassembles with an extra trailing comma. Reproducible with streaming enabled. Example from our side (reconstructed):

matt: ```json
{"response": {"id": "resp_01", "items": [
  {"name":"widget","qty":3},
],}}
```

matt: That extra comma is from our chunk joiner when partial array fragments end with a comma and the final chunk gets a stop token insert. Looks like a regression introduced in the canary's streaming fragmenter changes.

ryan: Ugh. We rolled the fragmenter change in v3p4 to improve throughput, but the boundary handling missed the case where arrays are emitted as N chunks and the last chunk includes a trailing comma token.

ryan: Immediate options: 1) rollback the canary for the affected customer (route their alias to r-inf-v3p3-stable), 2) offer a temporary client-side workaround (lenient JSON parse / ignore trailing commas), or 3) flip streaming=false for onboarding requests.

ci-bot: Deployment job id: deploy-20260310-5823 (canary apply). Status: SUCCESS. Canary subset: 5% traffic.

sophia: I can reproduce locally by hitting the canary with streaming chunks: copy/paste this repro (will fail with node's JSON.parse unless you strip trailing commas):

sophia: ```bash
curl -s -X POST https://canary.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"r-inf-v3p4-canary","input":"emit items array","stream":true,"json_mode":"strict"}'
```

sophia: Response chunks show the array fragments and occasionally end with a comma token. Also seeing ~8-12% token increase vs stable due to extra wrapper keys — customer billing spike possible.

eva: For the customer: suggested immediate mitigation = toggle their routing back to stable alias + we can issue credits for extra tokens while we diagnose. I'll propose rollback and ask PM for approval on credits.

matt: I'll open an urgent patch: fix streaming joiner to drop terminal commas and normalize wrapper usage. PR #4289. Trying hotfix to target canary edge within 1 hour. If hotfix not safe in time we should rollback the canary for all affected tenants.

ryan: I'll run the rollback command for Acme now: `redwoodctl route set acme-model-alias r-inf-v3p3-stable --force` and monitor.

ci-bot: Rollback for alias acme-model-alias started (job rollback-20260310-77).

customer-rep: Thanks — they asked for ETA on fix and whether this could affect other customers. They also flagged that their parser errors surfaced to end-users (bad UX) so they'd like escalation.

matt: Risk scope: only streaming=true + json_mode=strict customers on canary; canary at 5% so limited but incidents like Acme are hitting that subset. Hotfix PR linked; if QA green I'll promote to canary and we can monitor for absence of trailing commas.

sophia: QA notes: testcases added for chunk boundaries and wrapper normalization. Repro steps and expected normalized payload included in PR.

eva: I'll reply to Acme with rollback confirmation, credits offer, and ETA (hotfix in progress). Marking this thread high priority. :white_check_mark:

matt: tagging PR and issue: issue #6123, PR #4289. Will update when hotfix is merged or if rollback needs widening.

customer-rep: Appreciate fast turnaround. Please keep me posted in this thread and I'll relay to the customer.

ryan: monitoring logs for rollback: trace tr-8a9f2c4b should show requests routed to r-inf-v3p3 in ~2 minutes.

ci-bot: Rollback completed for acme-model-alias. All traffic to that alias now points to r-inf-v3p3-stable. Job rollback-20260310-77 SUCCESS.

eva: Confirmed with customer — parser errors gone after routing change. Leaving open until hotfix validated, then we'll close.

matt: Hotfix branch passing e2e in staging; will cut canary release in ~30m. If clean, we'll expand canary slowly.

sophia: After hotfix deployed, I'll run full regression suite and sample payloads from customers we saw failing.

eva: Closing loop with Acme and offering one week credit for token anomaly. Will update thread when final canary status is green. :handshake:
